newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqi journalists ask Uday to lead their union.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi journalists ask Uday to lead their union.

text.p: Iraqi journalists decided at a special meeting on Friday to ask President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday to accept the chairmanship of their union again.
Uday, still confined to a wheelchair following an assassination attempt in Baghdad in December, was the head of Iraqi Journalists Union for two sessions but gave up the post last year.

The current chairman, Taha al-Basri, told more than 1,000 journalists gathered in al-Rasheed theatre in Baghdad, that he was hopeful Uday would not turn down the request as "his leadership of the union will solidify its entity and consolidate its achievements."
Under Uday, Iraqi journalists got two salary increases and plots of residential land in provincial centres and in Baghdad.
Speaker after speaker hailed the decision to ask Uday to lead their union again. The audience clapped and chanted at every mention of Saddam.
Latest television footage showed Uday in a wheelchair, moving both hands at ease with his left leg still in bandages.
